# makes the (Latin) passphrase untypeable and locks the user out (#6229).

# own create-config leaves the file readable by root alone, and a config this
# user cannot read must not pass for one that wants its snapshots kept.

# Existing fingerprint setups have pam_fprintd first in /etc/pam.d/sudo and
# /etc/pam.d/polkit-1 but no lid gate, so a closed-lid sudo or pkexec would
# block on the unreachable reader for the full pam_fprintd timeout before
# offering the password. Insert a pam_exec gate before pam_fprintd that skips
# fingerprint while the lid is closed. New setups already get this from
# omarchy-setup-security-fingerprint.
#
# The gate points at the fixed /usr/bin path the omarchy package always
# provides, so it keeps working across package installs and dev-link (which
# overlays $OMARCHY_PATH but leaves /usr/bin untouched). pam_exec needs a
# literal absolute path — it does not expand env vars.

gate="auth      [success=1 default=ignore] pam_exec.so quiet /usr/bin/omarchy-hw-laptop-closed"

for pam in /etc/pam.d/sudo /etc/pam.d/polkit-1; do
  if [[ -f $pam ]] &&
    grep -q 'pam_fprintd\.so' "$pam" &&
    ! grep -q 'omarchy-hw-laptop-closed' "$pam"; then
    sudo sed -i "/pam_fprintd\.so/i $gate" "$pam"
  fi
done

echo "Tune reclaim for swap on zram"

# Everything here only applies the shipped config early; boot picks it up
# regardless. Nothing is worth failing the migration chain over, so each step
# falls back to asking for a reboot.

# Load our file specifically rather than --system, which returns nonzero for
# any invalid key in any admin sysctl file on the machine.
sudo sysctl -p /etc/sysctl.d/99-omarchy-sysctl.conf >/dev/null || true

if sudo systemctl daemon-reload; then
  # Resizing swaps the device off first, which faults every stored page back
  # into memory. That's only cheap while it's empty, so a device under
  # pressure keeps its old size until the next boot. A device that doesn't
  # exist yet reads as empty, which is what we want: the restart brings it up
  # against the unit daemon-reload just generated.
  zram_used=$(awk '$1 == "/dev/zram0" {print $4}' /proc/swaps)

    exit 0
  fi
fi

zram_dropin="${OMARCHY_ZRAM_DROPIN:-/usr/lib/systemd/zram-generator.conf.d/90-omarchy.conf}"

# Drop-ins outrank the main config file, so a leftover /etc copy decides nothing
# and only implies /etc is where zram gets configured.

# when nothing configures one, so until the drop-in lands the /etc copy is the
# only thing standing between this machine and no zram swap. The update pipeline
# installs packages before it runs migrations, but a dev checkout carries
# migrations from a release the installed package does not have yet.

echo "Only check for pending migrations at login, not on every package update"

# omarchy-update-user-notify.path watched /usr/share/omarchy/migrations, but
# pacman writes that directory during every update -- including the blessed
# `omarchy update`, which runs omarchy-migrate a step later. The watcher fired a
# critical notification for migrations that were already being applied in the
# visible update terminal. Retire the watcher and keep only the once-per-login
# check, now named after the command it runs.

wants_dir="$HOME/.config/systemd/user/graphical-session.target.wants"

systemctl --user daemon-reload >/dev/null 2>&1 || true

# The watcher's unit file is already gone, but it stays loaded in a session that
# started before this update, so stop it before it can fire again.
systemctl --user stop omarchy-update-user-notify.path >/dev/null 2>&1 || true

# Enable the replacement before dropping the old enablement, so a failure here
# can never leave a user with no notifier at all. Enable without --now: this
# usually runs from inside `omarchy update`, and starting the notifier here would
# pop a toast for the migrations running right after it -- the exact behavior
# being removed. `systemctl enable` also needs a live user manager, which
# `omarchy update` over SSH does not have, so fall back to writing precisely the
# symlink it would have written rather than silently doing nothing.
if ! systemctl --user enable omarchy-migrate-notify.service >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  mkdir -p "$wants_dir"
  ln -sfn /usr/lib/systemd/user/omarchy-migrate-notify.service \
    "$wants_dir/omarchy-migrate-notify.service"
fi

# Drop the retired enablement by hand instead of through `systemctl disable`.
# The package ships omarchy-update-user-notify.service as a compatibility
# symlink onto the new unit, for users who have not reached this migration yet,
# so disabling that name here would disable the replacement along with it.
rm -f "$wants_dir/omarchy-update-user-notify.path" \
  "$wants_dir/omarchy-update-user-notify.service"

systemctl --user reset-failed omarchy-update-user-notify.path >/dev/null 2>&1 || true

# restarted it and nothing noticed when it went away, so a single lost start
# left every ~/.XCompose sequence (CapsLock m s -> emoji) dead for the rest of

# session to start into. `systemctl enable` needs a live user manager, which an

echo "Drop Kvantum now that Qt apps follow the theme through the GTK platform theme"

# falls back to built-in Fusion and takes its palette from
# QT_QPA_PLATFORMTHEME=gtk3, which actually tracks the Omarchy theme. Kvantum

#
# kvantum-qt5 has to go in the same transaction: it is the only thing that
# requires kvantum, so removing kvantum alone fails the dependency check. It has
# been dead weight since VLC was retired anyway, and it takes qt5-svg and

echo "Repair theme symlinks the state-move migration left dangling"

# 1781043107.sh re-linked legacy theme symlinks whose targets were stored as a
# literal "~/.config/omarchy/current/..." string. The replacement used the same
# literal tilde, which the filesystem never expands inside a symlink target, so
# btop, Helix, and VS Code/Cursor would have lost their theme while the
# migration reported success anyway. That migration is already marked applied
# everywhere it ran, so this one repairs any link it left dangling.
#
# No shipped Omarchy code ever wrote these six targets with a literal tilde, so
# this is expected to be a no-op almost everywhere, and it stays deliberately
# narrow to keep it that way. Only a target that starts with a literal "~/" is
# repaired: the filesystem never expands one, so such a link cannot ever have
# worked, while a custom link into a dotfiles repo is a real path even when that
# repo happens to be unmounted right now.

relink_if_dangling() {
  local link="$1"
  local expected_target="$2"
  local target

  [[ -L $link ]] || return 0

  target=$(readlink "$link") || return 0

  # Already pointing at the state directory.
  [[ $target == "$expected_target" ]] && return 0

  # Still resolves, so it is a working link we have no business rewriting.
  [[ -e $link ]] && return 0

  # Only an unexpandable literal-tilde target naming this theme file is ours.
  case "$target" in
    "~/"*/omarchy/current/theme/"${expected_target##*/}") ;;
    *) return 0 ;;
  esac

  ln -sfn "$expected_target" "$link"
}
migrations.description: Repair theme symlinks the state-move migration left dangling

echo "Restore polkit brute-force protection on machines that enabled fingerprint or FIDO2 auth"

polkit=/etc/pam.d/polkit-1

# When fingerprint or FIDO2 auth was set up while /etc/pam.d/polkit-1 did not yet
# exist -- the normal case on Arch, where the polkit package ships its stack in
# /usr/lib/pam.d/polkit-1 -- the setup commands hand-rolled an /etc/pam.d/polkit-1
# that lists pam_unix directly instead of `include system-auth`. That override
# dropped pam_faillock, so polkit prompts had no brute-force lockout and their
# failures never counted toward the shared tally. The setup commands now defer to
# system-auth; this repairs the files the old ones already wrote.
#
# Only the exact stack those commands produced is touched. Every non-blank,
# non-comment line must be one of the known hardware-auth auth lines (the
# clamshell gate, pam_fprintd, or the FIDO2 pam_u2f line) or a bare
# `X required pam_unix.so`; all four bare pam_unix lines must be present; and
# system-auth must not already be included. This matches the fingerprint, FIDO2,
# combined, and post-removal (markerless, both remove commands strip only their
# own marker lines) layouts, and refuses any administrator-authored stack that
# carries other directives. The repair replaces only the bare pam_unix lines, so
# comments and the hardware-auth lines are preserved verbatim.

is_omarchy_vulnerable_stack() {
  local file=$1 line
  local re_gate='^auth[[:space:]]+\[success=1 default=ignore\][[:space:]]+pam_exec\.so quiet /usr/bin/omarchy-hw-laptop-closed[[:space:]]*$'
  local re_fprintd='^auth[[:space:]]+sufficient[[:space:]]+pam_fprintd\.so[[:space:]]*$'
  local re_u2f='^auth[[:space:]]+sufficient[[:space:]]+pam_u2f\.so cue authfile=/etc/fido2/fido2[[:space:]]*$'
  local re_bare='^(auth|account|password|session)[[:space:]]+required[[:space:]]+pam_unix\.so[[:space:]]*$'
  local phase

  # Already fixed, or partially converted: leave it alone (also makes reruns no-op).
  if grep -qE '^(auth|account|password|session)[[:space:]]+include[[:space:]]+system-auth' "$file"; then
    return 1
  fi

  # The vulnerable signature: all four phases delegated to a bare pam_unix.
  for phase in auth account password session; do
    grep -qE "^${phase}[[:space:]]+required[[:space:]]+pam_unix\.so[[:space:]]*\$" "$file" || return 1
  done
migrations.description: Restore polkit brute-force protection on machines that enabled fingerprint or FIDO2 auth

echo "Stop the boot from waiting on a black screen for the console to answer"

# systemd asks the console for its size when PID 1 starts and waits for the
# reply. With Plymouth holding the screen the reply sometimes never comes, and
# about 1 boot in 10 sits on a black screen until a key is pressed.
# omarchy-defaults.conf now carries systemd.tty.term.console=dumb, which makes
# systemd skip the query. The package has already written that file by the
# time this runs; the boot image still holds the old command line until it is
# rebuilt.

defaults_conf="${OMARCHY_LIMINE_DEFAULTS_CONF:-/etc/limine-entry-tool.d/omarchy-defaults.conf}"
running_cmdline="${OMARCHY_RUNNING_CMDLINE:-/proc/cmdline}"
rebuild_marker="${OMARCHY_LIMINE_REBUILD_MARKER:-/var/lib/omarchy/migrations/1791581004}"
modules_dir="${OMARCHY_KERNEL_MODULES_DIR:-/usr/lib/modules}"
limine_functions="${OMARCHY_LIMINE_FUNCTIONS:-/usr/lib/limine/limine-common-functions}"
param="systemd.tty.term.console=dumb"

# Whether a command line carries the parameter as systemd reads it: split on
# spaces, tabs and newlines outside single or double quotes, which it drops, the
# last assignment of the key winning, even one an unclosed quote runs to the end.
carries_param() {
  local cmdline=$1 word="" last="" quote="" char i
  for ((i = 0; i < ${#cmdline}; i++)); do
    char=${cmdline:i:1}
    if [[ -z $quote && ($char == '"' || $char == "'") ]]; then
      quote=$char
    elif [[ $char == "$quote" ]]; then
      quote=""
    elif [[ -z $quote && $' \t\n\r' == *"$char"* ]]; then
      [[ $word != "${param%%=*}="* ]] || last=$word
      word=""
    else
      word+=$char
    fi
  done
  [[ $word != "${param%%=*}="* ]] || last=$word
  [[ $last == "$param" ]]
}

omarchy-cmd-present limine-mkinitcpio || exit 0
migrations.description: Stop the boot from waiting on a black screen for the console to answer

# rebuilds the boot image when a drop-in changes, so an image built since
# plymouth updated still holds it.

mkinitcpio_conf="${OMARCHY_MKINITCPIO_CONF:-/etc/mkinitcpio.conf}"
conf_dir="${OMARCHY_MKINITCPIO_CONF_DIR:-/etc/mkinitcpio.conf.d}"
vconsole_conf="${OMARCHY_VCONSOLE_CONF:-/etc/vconsole.conf}"

# leaves the file out. Skip conservatively if evaluation fails.
added=$(bash -c '

  add_file() { echo added; }
  source <(cat -- "$1" "$2"/*.conf 2>/dev/null) || exit 1

# it does. timeout: 1 with quiet: yes makes the boot silent and

# Menu asks for it explicitly. Only machines that never set a timeout of
# their own get the new one: an uncommented timeout: is the user's and

echo "Write the bar's tray where the bar drew it"

# The bar used to draw the tray at the inner end of its section, whatever the
# layout said: first in the right section, last in the left and center ones,
# and only the last tray a section listed. It now draws every widget in the
# order the layout lists them, so the tray moves there in the layout, any
# other trays in the section go, and the bar looks as it did. This runs
# before the center section is split around its anchor (1791969355), as the
# bar pinned the tray before splitting it.
#
# A replacement bar (a clone of the built-in one, or a third party's) reads the
# layout the way it was written for, so its config is left as it is.
config_file="$HOME/.config/omarchy/shell.json"
if [[ -s $config_file ]] && jq -e '
  (.bar | type) == "object" and ((.bar.id // "" | tostring) | IN("", "omarchy.bar")) and (.bar.layout | type) == "object"
' "$config_file" >/dev/null; then
  tmp=$(mktemp)
  jq '
    def entry_id: if type == "object" then (.id // "" | tostring) else tostring end;
    def pin($first):
      if type == "array" then
        map(select(entry_id == "omarchy.tray"))[-1:] as $tray
        | map(select(entry_id != "omarchy.tray")) as $rest
        | if $first then $tray + $rest else $rest + $tray end
      end;

    .bar.layout |= with_entries(
      if .key == "right" then .value |= pin(true)
      elif .key == "left" or .key == "center" then .value |= pin(false)
      end
    )
  ' "$config_file" >"$tmp"
  if [[ $(jq -cS . "$tmp") != "$(jq -cS . "$config_file")" ]]; then
    mv "$tmp" "$config_file"
  else
    rm -f "$tmp"
  fi
fi
migrations.description: Write the bar's tray where the bar drew it

echo "Split the bar's center section at its anchor into centerBegin, center and centerEnd"

# The center section is now a box whose widgets are centered as one group, with
# centerBegin and centerEnd hanging off its two edges. centerAnchor named the
# one center widget pinned to the middle of the bar, with the rest flanking it:
# it stays in the box, and what flanked it moves to the sections either side,
# so the bar looks as it did. A center list without its anchor was centered as
# one group already, and stays whole in the box.
#
# A replacement bar (a clone of the built-in one, or a third party's) reads the
# layout the way it was written for, so its config is left as it is.
config_file="$HOME/.config/omarchy/shell.json"
if [[ -s $config_file ]] && jq -e '
  (.bar | type) == "object" and (.bar | has("centerAnchor")) and ((.bar.id // "" | tostring) | IN("", "omarchy.bar"))
' "$config_file" >/dev/null; then
  tmp=$(mktemp)
  jq '
    def entry_id: if type == "object" then (.id // "" | tostring) else tostring end;
    def list: if type == "array" then . else [] end;

    (.bar.centerAnchor | if type == "string" then . else "" end) as $anchor
    | (if (.bar.layout | type) == "object" then .bar.layout.center | list else [] end) as $center
    | (first(range(0; $center | length) | select($anchor != "" and ($center[.] | entry_id) == $anchor)) // null) as $index
    | if $index != null then
        .bar.layout.centerBegin = (.bar.layout.centerBegin | list) + $center[0:$index]
        | .bar.layout.center = [$center[$index]]
        | .bar.layout.centerEnd = $center[$index + 1:] + (.bar.layout.centerEnd | list)
      end
    | del(.bar.centerAnchor)
  ' "$config_file" >"$tmp"
  mv "$tmp" "$config_file"
fi

echo "Keep background selections across renumbered bundled backgrounds"

# Tokyo Night's backgrounds moved up a number when Liftoff took the lead, so
# 0-winding-road became 1-winding-road. A selection of a theme background whose
# name, and its WebP, are gone from the theme moves to the theme's one
# background with the same name under another number. A theme is its bundled
# backgrounds with a user theme of the same name laid over them, as
# omarchy-theme-set stages it. A background that still opens, a user's own
# backgrounds, and anything without exactly one match stay as they are. So does
# a name a symlink stands for: staging keeps some symlinks and not others (not
# those of a cloned theme), so it is left rather than guessed at.
current_dir="$HOME/.local/state/omarchy/current"
staged_backgrounds="$current_dir/theme/backgrounds"

# Prints the theme's file for a renumbered background name.
renumbered_source() {
  local theme="$1" name="$2" stem dir file found=""
  local -A seen=()

  [[ -n $theme && ${theme##*/} == "$theme" && $name =~ ^[0-9]+-(.+)\.[^.]+$ ]] || return 1
  stem=${BASH_REMATCH[1]}

  # The user theme first: its files shadow bundled ones of the same name.
  for dir in "$HOME/.config/omarchy/themes/$theme/backgrounds" "$OMARCHY_PATH/themes/$theme/backgrounds"; do
    # A symlinked backgrounds folder is not staged from a cloned theme.
    [[ ! -L $dir ]] || return 1
    [[ -e $dir/$name || -e $dir/${name%.*}.webp ]] && return 1
    for file in "$dir"/*; do
      [[ ${file##*/} =~ ^[0-9]+-(.+)\.[^.]+$ && ${BASH_REMATCH[1]} == "$stem" ]] || continue

echo "Clear SoundWire routes the retired N1x UCM profiles left in the saved mixer state"

# Omarchy's own MT8901 UCM profiles, replaced by NVIDIA's in 3a209895e4, routed
# PDI2 to DP3 (ASUS ProArt P14) and PDI7/PDI8 to codec ports (ProArt P14 and
# Dell XPS 16). alsactl saved those routes and restores them every boot, and
# NVIDIA's profiles only set the routes they use, so a host port ends up fed by
# two PDIs. The MT8901 SoundWire driver then rejects the 2-channel speaker and
# microphone streams with EINVAL, PipeWire drops the HiFi profile, and the
# internal speakers and microphones vanish. No current profile routes PDI7 or
# PDI8, or PDI2 to DP3, so those values can only be leftovers.
if ! omarchy-hw-aarch64-n1x; then
  exit 0
fi

card=mt8901soundwire
state_file="${OMARCHY_ALSA_STATE:-/var/lib/alsa/asound.state}"
card_path="${OMARCHY_PROC_ROOT:-/proc}/asound/$card"

# amixer can't find a card the user has no seat ACL for (an update over SSH),
# so ask the kernel whether it exists, and fail rather than complete unrepaired.
if [[ ! -e $card_path ]]; then
  exit 0
fi

amixer -c "$card" info >/dev/null

live_route() {
  amixer -c "$card" sget "$1" | sed -n "s/^  Item0: '\(.*\)'$/\1/p"
}

saved_route() {
  if [[ -e $state_file ]]; then
    awk -v card="state.$card" -v name="name '$1'" '
      /^state\./ { in_card = ($1 == card) }
      in_card && $0 ~ "^[ \t]*" name "$" { found = 1; next }
      found && $1 == "value" { print $2; exit }
    ' "$state_file"
  fi
}

rebuild_marker=/var/lib/omarchy/migrations/1794380120

if ! omarchy-hw-aarch64-qualcomm ||
  ! omarchy-hw-match-device-tree microsoft,surface-laptop-8-13p8 microsoft,surface-laptop-8-15; then
  exit 0
fi

sudo env PATH="$PATH" OMARCHY_PATH="$OMARCHY_PATH" bash -euo pipefail -c '
  source "$OMARCHY_PATH/install/hardware/microsoft/surface-laptop8.sh"
'

# A marker records the machine-wide rebuild: another user's run must not repeat
# it, while a missing marker still retries an interrupted rebuild.
if [[ ! -e $rebuild_marker ]]; then
  rebuild_log=$(mktemp)
  trap 'rm -f "$rebuild_log"' EXIT
  sudo limine-mkinitcpio 2>&1 | tee "$rebuild_log"

  # limine-mkinitcpio reports a kernel it could not rebuild and still exits 0.
  # That image lacks the early drivers, so the migration stays pending.
  if grep -q 'mkinitcpio failed for kernel' "$rebuild_log"; then
    echo "A boot image was not rebuilt. Fix the error above, then run omarchy-migrate again before rebooting." >&2
    exit 1
  fi

  sudo install -Dm644 /dev/null "$rebuild_marker"

fi
migrations.description: Set up the Surface Laptop 8 on installs made before its board setup

echo "Keep the legacy Super + Ctrl + X dictation toggle ahead of the new agents panel hotkey"

# Super + Ctrl + X now opens the agents panel. Hyprland runs every bind on a key,
# so the legacy dictation toggle 1793477875 wrote would fire alongside the panel.
# o.rebind replaces the default instead. That migration only added the toggle to
# a file with no other Super + Ctrl + X binding, appended at the end, so the
# rebind drops nothing personal, and it stays inside the dictation-installed
# check, so the panel keeps the key wherever that is false. Only that exact line
# is changed; bindings written by hand are left as written, like any personal
# binding that shares a key with a new default.
bindings="$HOME/.config/hypr/bindings.lua"
legacy='  o.bind("SUPER + CTRL + X", "Toggle dictation", "omarchy-dictation toggle")'

if [[ -f $bindings ]] && grep -qxF "$legacy" "$bindings"; then
  sed -i --follow-symlinks 's/^  o\.bind("SUPER + CTRL + X", "Toggle dictation", "omarchy-dictation toggle")$/  o.rebind("SUPER + CTRL + X", "Toggle dictation", "omarchy-dictation toggle")/' "$bindings"
fi
migrations.description: Keep the legacy Super + Ctrl + X dictation toggle ahead of the new agents panel hotkey

echo "Drop the Yaru icon theme, now that Files draws its own icons"

# Only Yaru itself goes: removing its dependencies as well (pacman -s) would
# take whatever arrived with it first. It stays where another package needs it.
if pacman -Qttq yaru-icon-theme &>/dev/null; then
  sudo pacman -Rn --noconfirm yaru-icon-theme
fi

# Setup linked Adwaita's back and forward arrows into Yaru for Nautilus, outside
# the package, and built an icon cache for them. Once Yaru is gone and no
# package owns the folder, clear exactly those and any folders left empty.
yaru=/usr/share/icons/Yaru
if [[ -d $yaru && ! -e $yaru/index.theme ]] && ! pacman -Qqo "$yaru" &>/dev/null; then
  for icon in go-previous-symbolic go-next-symbolic; do
    link="$yaru/scalable/actions/$icon.svg"
    if [[ -L $link && $(readlink "$link") == "/usr/share/icons/Adwaita/symbolic/actions/$icon.svg" ]]; then
      sudo rm -f "$link"
    fi
  done

  sudo rm -f "$yaru/icon-theme.cache"

  for dir in "$yaru/scalable/actions" "$yaru/scalable" "$yaru"; do
    if [[ -d $dir ]]; then
      sudo rmdir --ignore-fail-on-non-empty "$dir"
    fi
  done
fi

# GTK and Qt apps that named a Yaru colour, Omarchy's old default, get the
# Adwaita icons every theme uses now. An icon theme the user picked themselves
# stays, and so

qt_config="${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-$HOME/.config}/qtengine/config.json"
if [[ -f $qt_config && $(jq -r '.theme.iconTheme // empty' "$qt_config") == Yaru* ]]; then
